newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up, will rally stall?.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices up, will rally stall?.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices rose around one-quarter of a point in early afternoon trade, though the benchmark U.S. Treasury bonds drifted slightly off session highs amid concerns their latest rally might stall.
"It's kind of hard to buy into the market, dealers are a little more reluctant at this point, because Treasuries have stopped right here before," a trader said.

Treasury bonds criss-crossed a 6.85 percent yield, which was seen as posing resistance, though since the Federal Reserve last week decided the economy was not growing swiftly enough to require it to raise rates, prices have increased.
Activity in municipals was fairly brisk in the short-end and long-end of the primary markets.
New York City awarded $875 million of the $1.6 billion of revenue anticipation notes it sold to Merrill Lynch, with five firms winning the remainder.
The net interest cost for the notes that mature in April was 3.66 percent, and 3.80 pecent for the series that matures in June, when the cost of the letter of credit is not included.
Another competitive auction traders focused on was Pennsylvania's sale of $550 million of tax anticipation notes.
Goldman Sachs & Co won $250 million of the sale with a net interest cost of 3.739 percent.

Traders said that the market appears to be gaining confidence that the payrolls data for September, which are due on Friday, will be as soothing as some reports seen earlier this week, like the National Association of Purchasing Management index.
Economists surveyed by Reuters see employment gaining moderately, predicting an addition of 166,000 jobs.
December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade rose 15 ticks to 115-4/32, while U.S. Treasury bond futures gained 14 ticks to 110-11/32. This left the MOB spread at 153 ticks.

Traders speculated that the long-end of the municipal market, which has been supported by the view that supplies remain a bit light, might have drifted into the over-priced territory. "I think the long-end is quite expensive. I think serials are fairly valued," one trader said.
"The five- to 15-year sector actually is looking okay against the Treasuries; they look on the cheapside," he added.

Retail activity, which briefly surged after the U.S. central bank left interest rates changed at the last meeting of its policy-making body, evidently has abated, and traders saw few signs that bond funds were particularly active.

Actively quoted municipal issues included North Central Texas Health Facility at June 2021, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.82 percent NET, down two basis points from Friday's levels.
And Denver Colorado City and County Airport Revenues of November 2025, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 5.78 percent NET, down one basis point from Friday.
